editorial:
Imagine finding out at twenty that you only have a decade to live. That is exactly what happens to Matsuri, and it sets up a story that feels both heavy and hopeful. She decides to avoid the pain of heartbreak by staying away from romance, but life has other plans when she meets Kazuto. The vibe here is very soft and emotional, focusing on how people find meaning in the small moments when time is running out. You will feel like you are right there with them as they navigate their friendship and the scary reality of her illness.

The acting is what really sells this movie because the emotions feel genuine and not forced. While the story is a bit slow at times, the beautiful scenery makes up for it. If you enjoy stories that make you cry and think about your own life, you need to see this.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a heartbreaking note as Matsuri's health declines. She spends her final days surrounded by the people she loves, including Kazuto. After she passes away, Kazuto deals with the grief but finds comfort in the memories they shared. The story wraps up by showing that while her life was short, the love they had gave both of them a reason to keep moving forward and cherish every single day.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves tear-jerker romances and stories about life and death.
